schema_notes.r_hat: reward-model reward, recurrent_inference_vector at the candidate (depth-1 leaf)
schema_notes.gumbel_score: RECONSTRUCTED deterministic part of the mctx Sequential-Halving root score: uniform prior_logits + σ(completedQ), σ=(maxvisit_init+max_visits)·value_scale·minmax(Q), mctx defaults 50.0/0.1. The ±Gumbel(gumbel_scale) exploration noise is NOT reproduced — eval selection is visit-argmax, so this column diagnoses the systematic ranking only.
schema_notes.action_weight: mctx policy_output.action_weights over the K candidates
schema_notes.true_reward: TRUE one-step env reward from stepping a COPY of the env under the candidate vector (jit_batch_step_vector; trajectory state untouched)
schema_notes.rank_by: 1-based DESCENDING rank of the policy-argmax vector's signal value among the K candidates (rank 1 = best). When the prior IS in the set (policy-prior), r̂/v̂/Q use the prior's OWN in-set candidate row from the M=16 batched call (an in-set candidate can never rank > K); prior/visits use its candidate mass/visits. When the prior is ABSENT (dithered-book) the r̂/v̂/Q values are a SEPARATELY recomputed M=1 reference score (batched-vs-unbatched XLA differs ~1e-7, so a ranked-against-K reference can read K+1) and prior/visits are 0 (never sampled).
schema_notes.candidate_draw: the K-candidate set at each state is drawn with jax.random.fold_in(PRNGKey(eval_seed), k); the trajectory is the 848 policy-argmax replay (not an 835 search rollout), so there is no canonical 835-search draw to match — both are valid deterministic draws.
